solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sails across ocean and far away? No

indicators.note: the sails word is laid across the ocean word, so the one is split by the other

parts.note: sailcloth, canvas: sails are cloth
the sea is an ocean

explanation.surface: A traveller's question about sailing across the ocean to somewhere distant, answered with a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sails' is a noun standing for the material they are made of. The definition is a question answered 'No': not far away, so the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not far away is near, within easy reach, which is what the idiom means.

clue.text: Shelter companion who would exploit you?

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone sharing your shelter turns out to be a companion out to use you.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloodsucking parasite is the figurative term for a person who sponges off others.

clue.text: Cut off as sea is rising around cape

indicators.note: the upturned sea-and-is letters go around the cape letter
in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Ross Sea, off Antarctica
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A coastline cut off as the rising sea surrounds a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ROSSIS upwards to SISSOR in this down clue; the sea is the Ross Sea off Antarctica.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to snip with shears, so to cut off or out.

clue.text: Immobility making cattle incontinent!?

indicators.note: making the cattle be in the continent, so the cattle word is placed inside the other

parts.note: read as 'in continent': the continent is Asia, and its 'in' says the cattle go inside
kine is an old plural of cow

explanation.surface: A vet's diagnosis: the herd has stopped moving and lost bladder control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incontinent' must be split as 'in continent', doing two jobs: the continent is Asia and 'in' puts the cattle inside it. Kine is an archaic plural of cow.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the medical term for loss or impairment of voluntary movement.

clue.text: Rod Hull ultimately breaking elbow

indicators.note: the last letter of Hull breaks into the dismissal word

parts.note: to give someone the elbow is to sack, or axe, them

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Hull

explanation.surface: Rod Hull, the British entertainer with an Emu puppet, has hurt his elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Hull was a British TV entertainer; 'Rod' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaft a wheel turns on is a kind of rod or bar.

clue.text: Starts to dig in hard patch

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: strict, severe

explanation.surface: A gardener begins digging into a hard bit of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Patch here is an area or territory, like a police officer's beat.

clue.text: Sort of clip everything 3 list soldier put up

parts.note: all

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rota is a duty list
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An instruction to clip together a list for a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ROTAGI to IGATOR. The '3' gives no letters: it points to 3-down, scissors, an echo of a toothed clip.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring clip with toothed jaws used on electrical leads is named after the reptile's snout.

clue.text: They're safe in small doses but any stronger, unsafe

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are made unstable and rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that radiation is fine in small amounts but dangerous when stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsafe' tells you to rearrange ANY STRONGER; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: X-rays, named after their discoverer, are harmless at low exposure but damaging at high.

clue.text: Basic accommodation, one good toilet

parts.note: the Roman numeral I
loo, British slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A cheap lodging offers one decent toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A snow hut is very simple shelter, the most elementary of dwellings.

clue.text: F1 to cut major part of championship

indicators.note: the F1 letters cut into the influential word

parts.note: seminal, highly influential
F and the figure 1, which reads as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Formula One race being dropped from a large part of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'F1' looks like motor racing, but the 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The round before the final is one stage of a knockout tournament.

clue.text: Be humiliated if wrongly attired

indicators.note: the dressing word is set out wrongly, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning up in the wrong clothes is an embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to suffer abasement or accept insult meekly.

clue.text: Dog keeps barking as he's a hunter

indicators.note: the dog word holds the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go crazy and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hound keeps barking because he is a hunting dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' means mad, so AS HE'S is rearranged; 'a hunter' is French for a huntsman, also a light-cavalry soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: It is French for a huntsman, and also names a light-cavalry soldier.

clue.text: Religion might be this comical

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a faith could be found funny.
explanation.definitionFit: The faith of the Roman Church is a major Christian denomination.

clue.text: Express fury about priest being helpless

indicators.note: the fury word goes about the priest

parts.note: rant, rave angrily
Eli, the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone raging at a cleric who could do nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dependent on others implies an inability to cope alone.

clue.text: I'm in park, thinking

indicators.note: the I'm letters sit in the park word

parts.note: an estate, a park with grounds
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone pondering while sitting in the park.
explanation.definitionFit: A judgement or opinion, as in 'in my view', is a person's considered thinking.

clue.text: Part of an atmosphere inherent to motor racing

indicators.note: inherent to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The thrill of speed is an essential feature of a Grand Prix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'atmosphere' is the unit of pressure, not the mood of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of pressure equal to one 760th of a standard atmosphere.

clue.text: Temperature lost when old curtain breaks in shower unit?

indicators.note: the remaining letters break up and are rearranged
the temperature letter is lost from the curtain

explanation.surface: An old shower curtain breaks and the hot water goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T from CURTAIN, add OLD, and rearrange CURAINOLD. 'Shower unit' is not bathroom kit but the source of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloud bringing rain is the thing a shower comes from, playfully a unit.

clue.text: Territory somewhat hidden by cover

indicators.note: the somewhat phrase is hidden under the cover word, inside it

parts.note: a hat covers the head
a bit, slightly

explanation.surface: Land partly concealed beneath a covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural home area of an animal or plant is its territory.

clue.text: Seaside town offers attractions, perhaps, but only one hotel

parts.note: has, as a shop has or offers goods

indicators.note: of the two hotel letters, one is dropped so only one remains

parts.note: things, as in someone's thing being what attracts them
H is Hotel in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A resort with plenty to see but just one hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: HAS THINGS has two Hs; keep one. Hastings is a resort on the English south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a resort on the Sussex coast, famous for the 1066 battle.

clue.text: An easy goal centre-half gets with difficulty

parts.note: a tap-in is a simple goal from close range
CH is the football abbreviation for centre-half

explanation.surface: A defender scrapes in a simple goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means only just, if really necessary, so barely or with strain.

clue.text: Boat or, oddly, part of one

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: A, as in one item

explanation.surface: A boat, or a peculiar piece of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link here, not a choice between definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay sailing craft with an outrigger, much loved by setters.

clue.text: Knit circular shape enclosed by pocket

parts.note: purl is a knitting stitch, so to knit that way
O has a round shape
in, contained within

explanation.surface: Knitting instructions for a round motif sewn inside a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket something is to steal it, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Assistant starts to see more activity between the sheets

indicators.note: the starting letters sit between the bedding word's letters

parts.note: linen, bed sheets collectively

indicators.note: the first letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A saucy hint about an assistant getting busier in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a linesman is the referee's assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: The referee's assistant on the touchline is officially an assistant referee.

clue.text: Lead soldiers shy about lead soldiers

indicators.note: the throw word goes about the metal and army letters

parts.note: to shy is to toss or throw
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Toy lead soldiers thrown around a box of other lead soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition is the trick: first the military chiefs, then the metal and the gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest-ranking officers lead the troops, which is what the idiom names.

clue.text: Appears to understand writing

parts.note: see, as in 'I see'
MS, a manuscript

explanation.surface: Someone seems to grasp what is written.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to give an impression of being so.

clue.text: Dictionary invents new word to describe 'Liberals'

indicators.note: describe in its sense of drawing around, so the coining word encloses the party letters

parts.note: coins, as in coining a term
L is Liberal, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A dictionary makes up a new term for Liberal politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known British dictionary publisher, so a reference book by name.

clue.text: With no inner support, axes 'Banker from Hell'

indicators.note: only the outside letters of support remain once its inner letters go

parts.note: Y and X are graph axes

explanation.surface: A financier from the underworld who lops supports with axes.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' is a river, something with banks; this one flows through the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The river of the classical underworld has banks, so it is a banker of Hades.

clue.text: Consider weak recoil of gun acceptable

parts.note: thin, watery

indicators.note: a recoil kicks backwards, so the following words are turned round

parts.note: to gun an engine is to rev it
OK, all right

explanation.surface: A judgement that a feeble gun's kick is tolerable.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder something again carefully is to weigh or reflect on it.

clue.text: Golf lovers recalled upset

indicators.note: called back, so the letters are taken in reverse order

parts.note: G is Golf in the radio alphabet
nuts are fans, as in golf nuts

explanation.surface: Golf fans remembered being upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hurt by a remark leaves one wounded, upset in feelings.

clue.text: One blows it by running into shop

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, also called 'it'
X, the times sign, as in three by four

indicators.note: the letters run about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a chance by dashing into a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One blows it' reads as wrecking something; the definition is a wind player.
explanation.definitionFit: A jazz player blows into a reed instrument, so a musician who blows.
